ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, S.C. 2000, c. 17, and its Regulations; Canada Business Corporations Act, R.S.C. 1985, c. C-44, ss. 21.1 et seq. (federal individuals with significant control register); Quebec Business Corporations Act, CQLR c. mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified true copy of passport or national identity document of each director, officer, and beneficial owner holding 25% or more of voting rights or ownership interest
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public, commissioner for oaths, or corporate registry in the document's country of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of incumbency or corporate extract showing current directors and shareholders for any corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate registry or company secretary in the shareholder's jurisdiction of incorporation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: UBO disclosure declaration signed by each individual with significant control, including name, address, date of birth, nationality, and control structure
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public or licensed lawyer authorized to practice in Quebec
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille OR Consular Legalization if executed outside Canada; notarization only if executed in Quebec

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of existence / certificate of good standing for any foreign corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent corporate registry in the foreign shareholder's jurisdiction

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory customer due diligence must verify each director and UBO against a valid government-issued document; screening is required against the OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List, the UN Security Council Consolidated List, Global Affairs Canada sanctions lists under the Special Economic Measures Act, the Criminal Code terrorist entity list under s. 83.05, and FINTRAC's list of entities subject to asset freezes. Politically exposed persons (domestic and foreign) require enhanced due diligence, including source-of-wealth documentation and senior management approval. Screening records must be retained for at least five years after the completion of the business relationship.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) online reservation portal — https://www.registreentreprises.gouv.qc.ca
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under the Charter of the French Language, CQLR c. C-11, the corporate name must be in French; Latin-script transliteration is required, accents must be preserved, and any non-French element is permissible only as a recognized trademark or with prior authorization. The legal element must be in French, such as 'inc.' or 'corporation', and all pre-incorporation foreign-language documents must be filed with a certified French translation.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: No formal extension is available; the applicant may file a new reservation after expiry. If the Registraire rejects a proposed name, the applicant may file an administrative review request with the Registraire within 30 days of refusal, attaching the REQ decision number, a fresh name-search report, and a legal memorandum showing distinctiveness and lawful use. If the administrative review fails, the applicant may apply to the Superior Court of Quebec for judicial review under articles 529 et seq. of the Code of Civil Procedure within 60 days of the refusal. To avoid delay, a new name may be reserved immediately while the appeal is pending.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Conditionally permitted for this ISIC 6201 mobile utility software business: a virtual office may serve as the registered office only if it has a physical street address in Quebec, a person authorized to accept service during normal business hours, and is not a post-office box. A pure mail-forwarding address will not satisfy the statutory requirement. Commercial substance for tax purposes still requires actual local management and decision-making, and a virtual office alone is not sufficient to establish Quebec tax residence if all directors’ meetings and substantive business activities occur outside Canada.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low, approximately 1-5% per annum for a low-risk software issuer. Unannounced inspection may occur upon a customer complaint, failure to file annual declarations, or if the registered office is found to be non-functional. Bailiff service-of-process visits are possible but are not routine regulatory physical inspections. CRA tax audits are normally announced in writing.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act (Quebec), CQLR c. S-31.1, including sections 5-12 on incorporation and articles, sections 18-25 on the certificate and corporate capacity, and applicable provisions on directors, officers, shares, and corporate records; supplemented by the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, CQLR c. P-44.1.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec, Ministère de l’Emploi et de la Solidarité sociale
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of incorporation of a Quebec business corporation, generally filed through the Registraire des entreprises online service, together with the required initial declaration and name information.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital applies. Shares may be issued for cash, property, or services as permitted by the articles and the Business Corporations Act. Quebec does not require a statutory incorporation escrow account. The corporation must maintain adequate evidence of consideration received for issued shares and comply with applicable tax, accounting, and beneficial-ownership reporting requirements.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED that the Corporation accept the subscription by the incorporator or subscriber for the shares specified in the subscription agreement, against receipt of the agreed consideration. RESOLVED that the registered office of the Corporation be established at the Quebec address recorded in the corporate register, effective immediately. RESOLVED that [Name] be appointed President, [Name] Secretary, and [Name] Treasurer, each to serve until replaced or removed in accordance with the articles and applicable law. RESOLVED that the officers are authorized to execute all filings, banking documents, tax registrations, contracts, and other instruments necessary to commence business.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Confirm corporate jurisdiction, name, and eligibility
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec online services and the Nuans corporate-name search system where applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Choose a Quebec corporation under the Business Corporations Act or, alternatively, register a federal corporation extra-provincially. For the Quebec route, verify French-language naming requirements, obtain or confirm an acceptable corporate name, determine the registered office in Quebec, identify directors, and confirm the corporation's activities as software development and application operation rather than a regulated industrial activity.
required_dossiers: Proposed corporate name and French-language analysis
Nuans or other name-search report if required
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected, submit an amended name, a numbered-company alternative, or supporting evidence of name entitlement. Correct incomplete director, address, or language information before resubmission.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec online filing portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete and electronically submit the articles of incorporation and required initial declaration. Enter the corporate name, registered office, share provisions, restrictions, first directors, ultimate-person information where required, and principal business activities. Pay the prescribed Quebec filing fee in Canadian dollars. Notarization is generally not required for the statutory online filing; execute supporting instruments in accordance with the portal instructions and retain signed originals.
required_dossiers: Initial declaration or equivalent enterprise-register filing
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond through the REQ service channel within the stated cure period, correct the queried articles or declaration, and resubmit the filing with any additional evidence requested. If refused, request administrative review or file a corrected application.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain the certificate and activate corporate records
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec and the corporation's registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Download and retain the certificate of constitution, enterprise number, filed articles, and enterprise-register extract. Establish the minute book and securities register, record the registered office and directors, adopt bylaws, approve the share subscription, issue the shares, and document receipt of consideration. Record the beneficial ownership information required under Quebec law and maintain the records at the registered office or permitted records office.
required_dossiers: Securities register and share certificate or uncertificated-share record
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct corporate-record deficiencies by board or shareholder ratification where legally permitted, file any required amendment with the REQ, and preserve an audit trail explaining the correction.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Complete tax, payroll, and commercial registrations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency, Revenu Québec, and Commission des normes, de l’équité, de la santé et de la sécurité du travail
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for the federal business number and relevant CRA accounts, including corporate income tax, GST/HST, payroll, and import-export accounts where applicable. Register for Quebec corporate income tax, QST, source deductions, and employer obligations when thresholds or activities require registration. Assess whether employees, contractors, or Quebec payroll create CNESST obligations.
required_dossiers: Certificate of constitution and enterprise number
Business activity and expected revenue details
Payroll and employee information, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct account applications, provide requested identity or activity evidence, and request an effective-date adjustment or voluntary-disclosure treatment where permitted. Monitor filing deadlines while registration is pending.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Adopt operational governance and technology compliance controls
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporation's board and officers; Office of the Privacy Commissioner of Canada and Commission d’accès à l’information du Québec for applicable privacy oversight
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Approve banking authority, accounting policies, signing limits, financial reporting procedures, app-store agreements, intellectual-property ownership, privacy notices, consent mechanisms, cybersecurity controls, and data-retention procedures. For Quebec operations, assess Law 25 requirements under the Act respecting the protection of personal information in the private sector, including governance policies, privacy-impact assessments for qualifying transfers, and incident-response procedures.
required_dossiers: Privacy policy and terms of use
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Remediate identified governance or privacy gaps through board-approved corrective actions, updated policies, vendor controls, employee training, and documented breach-response measures.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable for ordinary mobile utility software development and digital application distribution. The principal corporate authority remains the Registraire des entreprises du Québec. Additional authorities may apply only if the business later operates regulated telecommunications, cloud infrastructure, construction, laboratory, or other physical facilities.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No general manufacturing, industrial operating, or software-production licence is required solely for developing and distributing a mobile utility application through Apple App Store or Google Play Billing.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministère de l’Environnement, de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques, de la Faune et des Parcs du Québec
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt for ordinary office-based software development and digital application distribution, provided no designated physical project, industrial facility, wastewater discharge, hazardous-material activity, or regulated construction is undertaken.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No activity-specific wastewater, VOC, or industrial-emissions thresholds apply to ordinary office-based software operations. Any leased premises must comply with applicable municipal waste, building, fire, and environmental rules. Separate authorization may be required for hazardous waste, significant wastewater discharge, fuel storage, backup generators, or data-centre infrastructure.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: No special industrial civil-defence or occupational clearance is required for ordinary software operations. The company must comply with Quebec occupational-health and safety requirements, including applicable obligations under the Act respecting occupational health and safety. If premises are occupied, obtain landlord or municipal confirmation of lawful occupancy, maintain required fire-safety measures, and address emergency exits, alarms, evacuation procedures, electrical safety, and workplace ergonomics. Structural-load inspections are required only where the premises, equipment, alterations, or municipal rules trigger them.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA/Agence du revenu du Canada) — federal income tax, payroll, and GST/HST administrative authority; taxpayer portal: CRA 'My Business Account' via canada.ca. For taxable supplies made in Quebec, Revenu Québec (Revenue Quebec) administers the GST/HST on behalf of the CRA under the federal–provincial single-administration agreement and levies the Quebec Sales Tax (QST/TVQ); portal: Revenu Québec 'Business' (revenuquebec.ca). The corporate register for a Quebec business corporation is the Registraire d'entreprise du Québec (registreentreprises.gouv.qc.ca).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Canadian-incorporated entities: a 9-digit federal Business Number (BN) and corporate income-tax account (RC) are assigned automatically upon articles of incorporation; a GST/HST (RT) account and, in Quebec, a QST (or NDT/TVQ) account are opened by registration with CRA/Revenu Québec (single-window registration). Foreign (non-resident) entities: (1) assess whether they carry on business in Canada or make taxable supplies in Canada; (2) apply for a BN using CRA Business Registration Online (BRO) with Form RC148 (non-resident request) or Form RC1, providing certificate of incorporation, foreign tax ID, and registered agent; (3) register for GST/HST through CRA or, in Quebec, through Revenu Québec's single registration (which assigns the QST number and the Quebec registration number (NEQ) for businesses); (4) obtain a CRA non-resident 'corporate income tax' account (RC) where the foreign entity has Canadian-source income from carrying on business in Canada; (5) file any required waiver/proof of permanent-establishment status. A non-resident digital supplier of software through Apple/Google platforms is generally not required to register for GST/HST/QST if the platform operator is itself registered and is the deemed supplier, but voluntary registration may be elected only when carrying on business in Canada and to recover input tax credits.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada, with foreign-exchange, financial-sector, anti-money-laundering, payments, and tax compliance administered or supervised as applicable by the Department of Finance Canada, the Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC), the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI), the Canada Revenue Agency (CRA), and the Financial Services Regulatory Authority of Ontario or Autorité des marchés financiers where provincial registration requirements apply.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada has a generally open foreign-exchange regime and the Canadian dollar is freely convertible for ordinary commercial, investment, dividend, interest, royalty, and service-payment purposes. Canada does not generally impose capital-account controls, mandatory conversion of foreign currency, exchange surrender requirements, or routine central-bank approval for non-resident ownership, equity funding, shareholder loans, intercompany payments, or profit repatriation. Banks must complete customer identification, beneficial-ownership, sanctions, source-of-funds, transaction-purpose, and anti-money-laundering reviews. Outbound dividends and other related-party payments remain subject to corporate-law solvency requirements, applicable withholding tax, treaty eligibility, transfer-pricing support, thin-capitalization and interest-limitation rules, GST/HST and income-tax compliance, and bank documentary review. Payments to sanctioned persons, prohibited counterparties, or jurisdictions may be blocked or reported. Large international electronic transfers and prescribed transactions may be reported by financial institutions to FINTRAC and CRA without imposing a currency-conversion restriction.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There is no general Canadian statutory deadline requiring export proceeds to be repatriated to Canada, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no general requirement to surrender foreign-currency export receipts to a Canadian bank or the Bank of Canada. Exporters may retain proceeds in foreign-currency accounts, subject to contractual, tax, accounting, sanctions, and anti-money-laundering obligations. Banks may request invoices, contracts, shipping or service-delivery evidence, and beneficial-owner information. The corporation must maintain accurate books and records, report taxable income and foreign assets or transactions where applicable, and respond to CRA, Statistics Canada, FINTRAC, or bank information requests. Specific goods, controlled technology, sanctions, customs, tax, or government-contract rules may create additional reporting or licensing obligations that are separate from foreign-exchange convertibility.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium for payment-collection and foreign-exchange services; Low for replacing a Canadian operating bank account or holding Canadian customer funds without the required authorization. An offshore electronic-money institution cannot rely solely on its foreign licence to provide unrestricted payment services, deposit-taking, retail payment activities, or money-services activities in Canada. Canadian operations may require registration under the Retail Payment Activities Act with the Bank of Canada, registration as a money services business with FINTRAC, provincial registration or licensing, contractual sponsorship by a regulated institution, and compliance with safeguarding, operational-risk, privacy, sanctions, consumer-protection, and reporting requirements. A foreign EMI may be used as a supplemental treasury or payout provider only after confirming Canadian legal perimeter, customer-fund segregation, settlement access, data-transfer, tax, chargeback, and account-closure risks. Apple and Google platform settlement accounts should be opened in the corporation's legal name where commercially available and reconciled to Canadian bank records.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: There is no universal federal requirement that directors physically appear at a bank branch to open a Canadian corporate account. Remote onboarding may be permitted after satisfactory electronic identity verification, document authentication, beneficial-owner verification, sanctions screening, and video or telephone review. Bank policy may require an in-person meeting, notarized or certified documents, Canadian-resident contact details, a local authorized signatory, or enhanced due diligence where directors, shareholders, source of funds, business activity, or operating geography is foreign. The corporation should expect verification of all directors, controlling shareholders, authorized users, and any individual owning or controlling 25 percent or more, subject to the financial institution's applicable identification rules and risk methodology.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Foreign parent, founder, director, or beneficial owner with complex ownership chains, nominee arrangements, trusts, or unexplained control rights.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified or bank-acceptable corporate registry extracts; articles and certificates of incorporation; complete ownership chart to natural persons; shareholder register; director register; trust deeds where relevant; beneficial-owner declarations; passports and residential-address evidence; board resolutions; shareholder agreements; explanation of control rights; and current organizational chart.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inability to demonstrate the commercial purpose of a mobile utility software and device-performance optimization application.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Product description; application-store listings; website and privacy policy; software-development agreements; platform agreements with Apple and Google; customer and vendor contracts; revenue model; projected transaction flows; expected currencies and countries; transaction-volume forecast; source-and-use-of-funds memorandum; and evidence that no regulated financial, gambling, virtual-currency, or remittance activity is conducted.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Incoming capital from an offshore shareholder, intercompany lender, investment fund, or multiple unrelated payors.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed subscription agreement or loan agreement; board and shareholder approvals; capitalization table; lender or investor ownership information; bank statements; audited or management accounts; source-of-wealth and source-of-funds evidence; wire-payment trail; tax characterization; repayment or dividend policy; and written explanation for any third-party funding.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-volume small-value card, app-store, foreign-currency, or cross-border receipts inconsistent with the stated low-risk business profile.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Processor and app-store settlement reports; customer geography analysis; refund and chargeback policy; merchant-account agreements; transaction-monitoring rules; anti-fraud controls; reconciliation reports; expected-volume model; sanctions-screening process; and evidence separating customer receipts from corporate funds.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Exposure to sanctioned, high-risk, embargoed, or unusually opaque jurisdictions and counterparties.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Counterparty master list; sanctions-screening methodology; beneficial-owner screening; geographic risk matrix; blocked-country controls; escalation procedures; payment approval logs; contractual restrictions; and independent compliance review.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Use of personal accounts, unlicensed payment intermediaries, offshore wallets, cash, or unsupported third-party payment instructions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Written treasury policy; approved-bank and approved-provider register; segregation-of-duties matrix; payment authorization policy; bank statements; reconciliation evidence; remediation plan; and proof that all future settlement flows will use accounts held in the corporation's legal name or a documented regulated collection structure.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Mismatch among registered office, management location, tax residence, banking location, operating staff, and payment-flow geography.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Quebec or federal corporate registration; lease or registered-office evidence; tax-residency analysis; management and payroll records; service-provider agreements; business-plan memorandum; explanation of remote operations; and confirmation of where strategic control, software development, customer support, and treasury functions are performed.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Incomplete tax, corporate, or regulatory records, including overdue Canadian returns or uncertain GST/HST and Quebec tax registrations.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: CRA and Revenu Quebec account confirmations; corporate tax filings; GST/HST registration or small-supplier analysis; Quebec sales-tax analysis; payroll registrations where applicable; annual corporate filings; financial statements; tax-clearance or good-standing evidence where available; and written remediation timetable.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Route equity subscriptions, paid-in capital, and shareholder loans through a Canadian corporate account held in the corporation's exact legal name. Use a regulated bank-to-bank wire, normally SWIFT MT103 or the bank's equivalent cross-border payment format, with complete ordering-party, beneficiary, intermediary-bank, invoice or agreement reference, and payment-purpose information. Canada does not generally require a universal foreign-exchange purpose code or prior central-bank approval for ordinary capital injections. The payment reference should clearly state the legal characterization, such as equity subscription, capital contribution, or shareholder loan, and should identify the relevant agreement and board approval. Maintain the subscription or loan agreement, corporate resolutions, capitalization records, source-of-funds evidence, beneficial-owner information, bank confirmation, and accounting entry. Avoid third-party funding unless pre-cleared by the bank. Confirm whether the remitting bank, intermediary, or Canadian receiving bank requires a foreign-investment, sanctions, tax, or regulatory declaration. Reconcile the incoming amount to the corporation's books and assess withholding, transfer-pricing, thin-capitalization, interest-limitation, and foreign-reporting consequences before any onward transfer.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Use the Canadian operating account or foreign-currency account for legitimate vendor, contractor, cloud-service, software-licence, advertising, app-store, payroll, tax, and other business payments. Standard low-value and ordinary commercial settlements may use SWIFT MT103, correspondent banking, card acquiring, ACH-equivalent arrangements, or bank-supported local payment rails. Commercial letters of credit may be issued or advised through a Canadian bank using SWIFT trade-finance messaging and should be governed by the agreed rules, typically UCP 600 for documentary credits and applicable International Standard Banking Practice. Documentary collections may use URC 522 where appropriate. Maintain contracts, purchase orders, invoices, delivery or service evidence, beneficiary verification, sanctions screening, tax treatment, and approval records. For digital-platform settlements, reconcile Apple and Google reports, gross receipts, commissions, refunds, withholding, chargebacks, and net bank credits. There is no general Canadian requirement to use a letter of credit or a prescribed payment rail for ordinary software exports or imports.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable foreign-exchange forwards with an authorized Canadian bank or appropriately regulated dealer, documented against forecast or committed Canadian-dollar, United States-dollar, euro, or other currency exposures.

Non-deliverable forwards where settlement in a convertible reference currency is commercially appropriate and the transaction is entered into with a regulated counterparty under documented master terms.

Currency swaps or cross-currency interest-rate swaps for documented funding or recurring currency exposures, subject to counterparty credit limits, collateral terms, accounting treatment, and applicable derivatives documentation.

Foreign-exchange options or collars may be used for risk-limited protection where the corporation understands premium, exercise, liquidity, and accounting consequences and the dealer confirms suitability.

Use ISDA or equivalent master documentation where required, establish board-approved hedge limits, prohibit speculative trading, maintain hedge-designation and valuation records, and reconcile derivative confirmations to underlying exposures. Dealer onboarding may require corporate authority, financial statements, beneficial-owner evidence, net-worth information, and a derivatives appropriateness assessment.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Quebec Annual Declaration (Déclaration annuelle) including ultimate beneficial ownership confirmation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (Quebec Enterprise Registrar)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after the anniversary of the enterprise's registration in Quebec
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late fees accrue on the unpaid declaration fee; continued non-filing may cause the Registrar to mark the enterprise inactive and, after 12 months of inactivity, administratively dissolve the corporation, resulting in loss of legal personality.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Federal Annual Return under the Canada Business Corporations Act (CBCA)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporations Canada, Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after each anniversary of the date of incorporation or of the corporation's registration under the CBCA
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file for two consecutive years may lead to administrative dissolution of the corporation under the CBCA; directors and officers may be subject to penal notices and personal liability for corporate obligations.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after the corporation's fiscal year-end; for a calendar-year corporation, no later than June 30 of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of 5% of the unpaid balance, plus 1% per month for up to 12 months; repeat failures may incur a 10% penalty; arbitrary assessments and interest apply.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after the corporation's fiscal year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of 5% of the unpaid balance if taxes are due; on recurrence, 10%; daily compounded interest applies until the return is filed and any indebtedness is settled.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No mandatory annual audit for a private business corporation in Quebec based solely on revenue or asset thresholds. A statutory audit is required only if the corporation is a distributing corporation for securities law purposes, its shares are listed or publicly held, or shareholders holding at least 5% of the voting shares request an audit under the Quebec Business Corporations Act. Third-party requiring audited financial statements may also impose an audit obligation.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) for publicly accountable enterprises; Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises (ASPE) permitted for private corporations. A private business corporation in Quebec may choose either IFRS or ASPE consistently.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: At each anniversary, the corporation must reconfirm in its Quebec Annual Declaration the current ultimate beneficial owners of shares carrying control rights. Any share transfer or change in significant control must be recorded in the internal register of individuals with significant control within statutory notice periods and the ownership picture reconfirmed with the Registrar on the next annual declaration. Failure to maintain or disclose UBO information is an offence subject to fines.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (Shareholders) and Share Transfers
Register of Individuals with Significant Control (Ultimate Beneficial Ownership Register)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: $500 - $900 per year for a registered office or registered agent service in Quebec ($700 - CAD $1,200)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: $12,000 - $30,000 for a certified independent audit of a development-stage mobile app company; zero if the audit is waived by unanimous shareholder consent

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: Federal 15% + Quebec 11.5% = combined 26.5% general corporate rate on taxable income above the small business threshold. Canadian-controlled private corporation (CCPC) claiming the Small Business Deduction: federal 9% + Quebec 4% (Quebec rate reduced to 3.2% for 2024 and subsequent taxation years under the Quebec Budget 2024-2025) = combined 12.2% to 13% on the first CA$500,000 of active business income. Non-resident-controlled Canadian corporations are not CCPCs and cannot claim the SBD.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: SR&ED Investment Tax Credits: CCPC receives a 25% refundable federal ITC on qualified Canadian R&D expenditures up to CA$3,000,000 (non-CCPC 15%); Quebec adds a refundable R&D tax credit of 30% for CCPCs on the first CA$3,000,000 of qualified expenditures (14% above the cap). Federal Patent Box-type deduction of 50% of qualifying patent income applies to taxation years beginning after 2024; Quebec offers an equivalent innovation/patent income deduction. Mobile utility app development qualifies as SR&ED only where systematic investigation is performed to resolve technological uncertainty; routine app maintenance, UI polish, or ordinary performance tuning is not qualifying expenditure.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: 20-year carryforward for non-capital losses and 3-year carryback under ITA s. 111(1); capital losses carry forward indefinitely but only against capital gains. The 5-year template limit is not applicable in Canada.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return (federal), filed with the Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) through the T2 EFILE program using CRA-certified software or the CRA My Business Account portal; paper filing is permitted in limited circumstances.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual. A fiscal period may not exceed 53 weeks; the fiscal year-end may differ from the calendar year, and the first fiscal period may be up to 371 days.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Return due no later than 6 months after fiscal year-end (e.g., December 31 year-end due June 30). Balance-due tax payable within 2 months after year-end generally, extended to 3 months for CCPCs eligible for the Small Business Deduction; large corporations whose taxable capital employed in Canada exceeds CA$15,000,000 remit monthly installments, while eligible CCPCs may remit quarterly.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net business income from mobile app operations for the fiscal period, net of deductible expenses and after app store platform commissions from Apple IAP and Google Play Billing; all worldwide income of a tax-resident Canadian corporation is reportable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident corporation files the T2 only if it carries on business in Canada through a permanent establishment; app-store sales to Canadian users through a foreign parent or foreign affiliate do not of themselves create a permanent establishment, but any Quebec-based employees, servers, or contract-development substance should be analyzed under the Canada-Quebec allocation rules and the tax treaty of residence.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net income after the deduction of loss carryovers, inter-corporate dividends, and Part I adjustments; this amount feeds the federal tax computation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a non-resident with a Canadian permanent establishment, taxable income is the income attributable to that permanent establishment as allocated under the Act and the applicable treaty; apportionment factors must be supported by contemporaneous records.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computes Part I tax at 38% less the 10% provincial abatement and 13% general rate reduction, resulting in the 15% general rate; CCPCs claim the Small Business Deduction here on the first CA$500,000 of active business income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A corporation that is not Canadian-controlled (i.e., controlled by non-residents) cannot claim the Small Business Deduction; the general 15% federal rate applies on all Canadian and foreign-source taxable income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Claims of SR&ED refundable and non-refundable investment tax credits, including the 25% CCPC credit on qualifying expenditures up to CA$3,000,000 and the 15% non-CCPC rate.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident corporation is generally ineligible for Canadian SR&ED ITCs unless it has a permanent establishment in Canada and carries on a business therein; credit claims require a completed Form T661 and detailed project technical summaries.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Technical narrative, expenditure pool computation, and project-by-project description of eligible research; requires supporting contemporaneous time sheets, payroll records, and technical memoranda.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Where mobile-app development is performed in Quebec for a non-resident parent, the allowance must be computed only for Canadian-based employees and qualifying Canadian expenditures; cross-border contracting segments are excluded.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: T106 – Information Return on Non-Arm's-Length Transactions with Non-Residents
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Mandatory disclosure of reportable transactions, including intercompany royalties, service fees, cost sharing, or IP transfers with related non-resident persons, where the aggregate annual value exceeds CA$1,000,000.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident controlled Canadian corporations file the T106 with respect to transactions with the foreign parent, affiliates, or shareholders; late filing carries penalties of CA$100 per day up to CA$2,500 per failure, increased penalties for counselling, plus gross-negligence transfer-pricing penalties under ITA s. 247(3).

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: 5% of unpaid balance plus 1% of the unpaid balance for each full month late, to a maximum of 12 additional percentage points. Interest at the CRA prescribed rate (currently approximately 9% annually for corporate deficiencies) is compounded daily on unpaid tax and installments. Gross negligence penalties for knowingly or under circumstances amounting to gross negligence making false statements: 50% of the understated tax. Criminal tax evasion under ITA s. 239(1) attracts fines of 50% to 200% of the evaded tax and imprisonment of up to 5 years.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: CO-17 – Corporation Income Tax Return (Quebec provincial), filed with Revenu Quebec through the Cliquez Affaires electronic filing service using Revenu Quebec-certified software or the Mon Dossier d'Entreprise portal.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual, aligned with the federal fiscal period.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Due within 6 months after fiscal year-end; Quebec balance-due payable within 2 months (3 months for a CCPC quebecoise eligible for the deduction pour petite entreprise). The general Quebec corporate rate remains 11.5%.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Records the corporate name, Quebec Enterprise Number (NEQ), business number, fiscal year-end, registered office address, and principal business activity (NAICS 511210), and identifies whether the corporation is a CCPC, a public corporation, or a non-resident controlled corporation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident-controlled corporation must indicate its non-resident control status, its Canadian permanent establishment presence, and the Quebec-allocated share of income; a Quebec-incorporated company without a physical Quebec establishment must nonetheless file as a Quebec-resident corporation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reconciles with the federal T2 business income line; includes gross app-store receipts, cost of goods sold, development wages, marketing, and platform commissions; the same deduction and income recognition rules apply as under the federal Act.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a non-resident corporation with a Quebec establishment, only income allocable to the establishment is taxable in Quebec; the allocation rules follow the federal/Quebec agreement and the relevant tax treaty.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: CO-17 – Deduction pour petite entreprise (small business deduction)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Claims the Quebec small business rate (4%, reduced to 3.2% for 2024 onward) on the first CA$500,000 of active business income of a Quebec-based CCPC, subject to the same CA$15,000,000 taxable-capital phase-out used federally.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A corporation controlled by non-residents is ineligible for the deduction pour petite entreprise; the 11.5% general Quebec rate applies.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: CO-17 – Crédit d'impôt recherche et développement
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Claims the refundable Quebec R&D credit (30% for eligible CCPCs on qualifying expenditures up to CA$3,000,000; 14% for other corporations) for Quebec-based app development research; claim requires supporting technical descriptions and Revenu Quebec approval of pre-claim forms where applicable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident corporation without a Quebec establishment may not claim the provincial R&D credit; wages must be attributable to employees performing R&D in Quebec.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: CO-17 – Schedule of transactions with non-resident related parties
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Discloses intercompany agreements, royalty payments, management fees, and transfer-pricing adjustments made by the Quebec corporation with foreign related parties, consistent with the federal T106.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The Quebec corporation must attach the same arm's-length analyses used federally; the absence of contemporaneous documentation exposes the taxpayer to reassessment and provincial penalties.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty: 5% of unpaid Quebec tax plus 1% per full month late, up to 12 months; interest at the Revenu Quebec prescribed rate compounded daily. False statements or omissions: 50% gross negligence penalty of the understated provincial tax; criminal prosecution under Quebec tax legislation may attract fines from 50% to 200% of the evaded tax and imprisonment of up to 5 years.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% statutory withholding under Part XIII of the Income Tax Act (ITA s. 212(2)) on dividends paid by a Canadian-resident corporation to non-resident shareholders. Quebec does not impose a separate provincial withholding tax on dividends.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The non-resident beneficial owner must: (1) obtain an official Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) from its tax residence authority (e.g., IRS Form 6166 for US residents or the equivalent from other treaty jurisdictions); (2) complete and provide the applicable CRA treaty declaration form (Form NR301 for hybrid entities, NR302 for US LLCs, or NR303 for disregarded entities) or otherwise substantiate entitlement; (3) deliver the TRC and declaration to the Canadian paying corporation before the dividend payment so that the reduced treaty withholding rate is applied at source; (4) ensure the ownership and limitation-on-benefits clauses are satisfied (e.g., the Canada-US treaty 5% rate requires a company that beneficially owns more than 10% of the voting shares); and (5) if excess tax was withheld, file a Part XIII refund claim with the CRA within two years after the end of the calendar year of the payment. For Quebec, no separate Revenu Quebec approval is required for dividend withholding.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory rates: interest 25% and royalties 25% under Part XIII, subject to exemptions for arm's-length interest not participating in the borrower's business. Treaty rates: under the Canada-US convention, interest is generally 0% in an arm's-length context, software copyright royalty is 0%, and patent/technical know-how royalty is 10%; most other Canadian tax treaties provide 10% for royalties and 10%-15% for interest. Apple IAP and Google Play Billing platform commissions paid to non-resident distributors are service fees, not royalties or interest, and are not subject to Part XIII withholding.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: The mandatory Canadian T106 information return threshold is CA$1,000,000 in aggregate non-arm's-length cross-border transactions for the taxation year. The Country-by-Country Report obligation applies to multinational groups with consolidated revenue of at least CA$750,000,000. Canada has not codified OECD-style Local File/Master File monetary thresholds, but the CRA requires contemporaneous transfer-pricing documentation prepared to OECD standards for any material intercompany transaction, with the level of documentation proportionate to the risk and complexity.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: CUP, Resale Price, Cost Plus, TNMM, Profit Split
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Canada does not maintain 'Economic Substance Regulations' comparable to offshore ESR regimes; economic substance is instead enforced through (i) central management and control tests for residency, (ii) permanent establishment attribution rules under ITA s. 115 and OECD PE principles, (iii) the General Anti-Avoidance Rule under ITA s. 245, and (iv) anti-treaty-shopping and beneficial-ownership jurisprudence (e.g., Alta Energy). A Quebec mobile app company must maintain real and demonstrable substance: Quebec-based developers and product managers, board meetings and decisions in Canada, ownership of IP in Canada, and a commercial rationale for any offshore intercompany arrangements. A 'mailbox' or invoice-only Quebec corporation with no employees or operational substance is exposed to recharacterization, denial of treaty benefits, and GAAR reassessment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion – suppression of app-store revenue
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to record Apple IAP and Google Play Billing settlement statements in the accounting records; maintaining undisclosed foreign bank accounts; issuing fictitious deductible invoices to reduce taxable income; or intentionally omitting Quebec TVQ/GST/HST obligations in connection with app monetization.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal tax evasion under ITA s. 239(1) and parallel Quebec legislation: fine of 50% to 200% of the tax evaded and imprisonment up to 5 years. Civil gross negligence penalty of 50% of the understated tax under ITA s. 163(2), plus compound daily interest at the CRA prescribed rate.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who participated in, assented to, or acquiesced in the omission may be jointly assessed; under ITA s. 227.1 directors are personally liable for unremitted employee source deductions and GST/HST; criminal prosecution may result in travel bans as bail conditions, asset freezes, and imprisonment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Failure to file returns and remit installments
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to file the T2 or CO-17 within 6 months after fiscal year-end; failing to remit balance-due installments; repeated non-compliance despite CRA or Revenu Quebec demand letters.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Late-filing penalty of 5% of the unpaid balance plus 1% per month up to 12 months, compounded with daily interest; Revenu Quebec imposes an equivalent penalty regime; continued default can trigger a CRA requirement to confirm, and ultimately a tax collection writ, garnishment, and seizure of corporate and personal assets.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are personally liable for unremitted federal and provincial source deductions, GST/HST/TVQ, and in Quebec for unpaid corporate taxes where the corporation's failure to file results in a willful default; the CRA may issue director liability assessments without first pursuing the corporation.
